subject: general
question: Which subatomic particle was discovered by J. Chadwick in 1932?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Neutron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Neutron** was discovered by the British physicist **James Chadwick** in **1932**. He performed an experiment where he bombarded **Beryllium** with **alpha particles**, which resulted in the emission of a new type of radiation consisting of uncharged particles.
 
• A **neutron** is a subatomic particle that has **no net electric charge** (it is neutral) and a mass slightly larger than that of a **proton**. ***Hence, the option identifying the neutron as Chadwick's discovery is correct.***
 
• Neutrons are located in the **atomic nucleus** along with protons. The number of neutrons in an atom's nucleus determines the **isotope** of that element.
 
• The mass of a neutron is approximately **1.6749 × 10^-27 kg**, or about **1.00866 atomic mass units (amu)**. Because they lack charge, they can easily penetrate the nuclei of other atoms, making them essential for **nuclear chain reactions**.
 
• For this monumental discovery, **James Chadwick** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1935**. His work led to a deeper understanding of the atomic structure and paved the way for the development of nuclear energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electron:**

 
 
• The **electron** was the first subatomic particle to be discovered. It was identified by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** through his experiments with **Cathode Ray Tubes**.
 
• It carries a **negative electrical charge** of approximately **-1.602 × 10^-19 Coulombs** and has a very small mass (about 1/1836th of a proton).
 
 
 
• **Proton:**
 
 
• The **proton** is a positively charged particle found in the nucleus. While **Eugen Goldstein** observed canal rays in **1886**, **Ernest Rutherford** is credited with the discovery of the proton in **1917** (and naming it in **1920**) after his experiments with nitrogen nuclei.
 
• The number of protons in the nucleus defines the **atomic number** and the identity of the chemical element.
 
 
 
• **Alpha Particle:**
 
 
• An **alpha particle** consists of **two protons** and **two neutrons** bound together, making it identical to a **Helium-4 nucleus**.
 
• They are emitted during **alpha decay** of radioactive substances. **Rutherford** used these particles in his famous **Gold Foil Experiment** to discover the atomic nucleus.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Nucleus:** Discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** in **1911**. It contains almost all of the atom's mass in a very small volume, composed of **nucleons** (protons and neutrons).
 
• **Subatomic Stability:** Neutrons act as a "glue" in the nucleus; the **strong nuclear force** between neutrons and protons overcomes the electrostatic repulsion between positively charged protons, keeping the nucleus stable.
 
• **Applications:** The discovery of the neutron was crucial for the **Manhattan Project** and the subsequent creation of nuclear reactors. Neutrons are used in **neutron diffraction** to study the structure of materials and in **cancer therapy** (Boron Neutron Capture Therapy).
